A bare percent pair or nondirective percent-brace line after the header is a native comment through before LF. usecase.md#whitespace-comments-and-directives-in-every-context: Common comment regions are recognized in all contexts, including strings, metadata, JSON, and accessibility blocks. They can remove entire comment lines and preceding blank lines. Native comments are different: only default context recognizes a physical line whose prefix before %% contains ASCII spaces/tabs only. Its mark is %% and its value runs through the physical line, excluding LF; neither U+2028 nor U+2029 ends it. A bare %% or a non-directive %%{...} line after the header is a native comment. Native comments supply a comment line, not an inline statement suffix.

Rule 13: stereotype-open: <<; enter stereotype context. take all characters through immediately before the first `>>`, provided that text contains no physical line break and is not all common whitespace. Stereotype interiors are text; a closer inside a directive does not end the unit. usecase.md#ordered-default-context-rules: **stereotype-open**: <<; enter stereotype context.

Stereotype text runs through before the first double angle closer. A separator-led comment ends the current value run while the stereotype context remains open. usecase.md#stereotype-context: Try `>>` first and return to default context. Otherwise take all characters through immediately before the first `>>`, provided that text contains no physical line break and is not all common whitespace. Then the closer is tried at its next position. On failure the unclosed-text fallback consumes a maximal non-LF run and leaves the context; the grammar rejects that fallback. Thus empty, whitespace-only, multiline, and unclosed stereotypes are rejected. U+2028/U+2029 can be text; nested `<<`, quotes, braces, punctuation, and backslashes are ordinary content. common.md#comment-lines: Comment lines are recognized independently of the diagram's syntax and of the context the lexer is in.
